13.0.0.en: Herod the Great rebuilt the temple in Jerusalem, and made it a splendid building, in the year 15 B.C. And its completion came in the year 64 A.D., and it had stood for about five centuries since the time of Ezra. Herod did not build it in honor of God, but to please the Jews. And Christ's prophecy about it was fulfilled in the year 70 A.D. at the destruction of Jerusalem and the demolition of the temple.

13.0.1.en: And as Christ was leaving the temple with His disciples, one of the disciples spoke - with pride - of the greatness of the temple's construction and the size of its great stones. So Christ took advantage of this remark to begin directing His talk about the destruction of Jerusalem and the demolition of the temple and its passing away, and in this there is more than one meaning and symbol:

13.0.2.en: (1) The demolition of the temple: it means the end of the era of animal sacrifices, and the beginning of the age of the Church, whose sacrifice is Christ Himself, and not the blood of goats.

13.0.3.en: (2) The demolition of the temple: it also means the death of our old man by Baptism, and the resurrection of our new spiritual man. (3) The demolition of the temple: it teaches us not to be dazzled by the glories of the world however great they may appear, because everything on earth has an end, but what is in heaven remains and is eternal.

13.1.0.en: The Mount of Olives lies east of Jerusalem, and because of its height the whole city can be seen, and the temple clearly as well. And when Christ and the disciples sat down, four of them came to Him, asking about the signs of the happening of what He had spoken of - the demolition of the temple. And St. Matthew adds in (Mt 24:3) that they also asked Him about His second coming and the end of the age, because they considered it one event, as was pointed out in the introduction to this chapter.

13.1.1.en: As for the Lord Christ, He began His important talk to the disciples by warning them of the appearance of false people who claim to be the Christ, or messengers from Him, and who will be a cause of the straying and destruction of many; so the Church in all her ages must beware of them.

13.1.2.en: It is noticed that the Lord Christ, in His talk about the signs, did not specify times. And the Church also teaches us the same teaching, not to be occupied with times but with repentance and preparation.

13.2.s.en: (3) Afflictions that will meet the disciples and the believers before the destruction of Jerusalem

13.2.0.en: The Lord Christ here tells the disciples of some difficult matters that will meet them and the believers in the period between His ascension and the destruction of Jerusalem, a period full of wars and informing against them, for they will be exposed to trials before the councils and synagogues of the Jews, and because of Him they will be beaten. But all this will be an opportunity for the disciples to bear witness to their faith before those who try them ... and notice that this is exactly what happened in the stoning of Stephen (Acts 7:59), the killing of James and the imprisonment of Peter (Acts 12:2 and 4), and others.

13.3.0.en: And before the destruction of Jerusalem also, the news of the preaching and the Gospel will be carried to all the surrounding nations, either because the disciples began the work of preaching outside Judea, or because of the Jews who come to Jerusalem in the days of Passover and return to their countries with the news of the preaching, as happened with the Ethiopian eunuch (Acts 8:27-39).

13.3.1.en: This is in regard to the destruction of Jerusalem, but in regard to the signs of the end of the world, the Christian faith will spread in the world, and many will believe before the second coming.

13.4.0.en: The Lord Christ here reassures His disciples lest they fear what is coming upon them, for He assures them that the Holy Spirit will never leave them in what they will be exposed to, so they should not worry before the trials and interrogations and not be troubled, because the Holy Spirit Himself will give them wisdom and boldness, so they must obey and speak what the Spirit dictates to them.

13.5.0.en: And because of the new faith, one house will be divided against itself, so that unbelieving children may kill their fathers who have believed and vice versa, and likewise a brother with his brother.

13.6.0.en: Believers in every generation await what Christ foretold to His disciples here, for whoever wishes to live in striving to please God and to preach in the name of Christ, Satan will usually raise many enemies around him... But look, my brother, in hope, at the faithful promise of Christ, for whoever endures these afflictions with patience has eternal salvation, indeed compensation for all he suffered (Rev 21:4). So take courage, my friend, before what meets you, for you are in a covenant with the One who promised.

13.7.s.en: (4) The events of the destruction of Jerusalem and the advice to flee

13.7.0.en: "The abomination of desolation": Daniel prophesied in (Dan 9:23-27) that after the lifting up of the Christ, a prince would come who would destroy Jerusalem and the temple, and abolish the sacrifices and the offering. And the word "abomination" means "uncleanness" accompanying this destruction, that is, what Daniel prophesied and Christ confirmed.

13.7.1.en: For from the year 66 A.D., Jerusalem was exposed to three Roman sieges, which ended in its storming in the year 70 A.D. at the hands of Titus, who demolished many parts of the temple, and entered it with his idols and images, so it was defiled by them, and indeed the offering of sacrifices in the temple was abolished from that time.

13.7.2.en: "Let him that readeth understand": a phrase Christ added to His words because He knows that the Gospel will be written and preached among the Gentiles. And the Lord Christ warns of the severity and terrors of the events at that time, so He gives the advice that everyone who is in Jerusalem and the surrounding regions at that time should flee to the tops of the mountains to escape the Roman siege.

13.8.0.en: These verses depict the severity and woes of this destruction, and advice for whoever wants to escape with his life from this devastation. Whoever is on the housetop, let him flee quickly and not think of his belongings in the house, for there will be no time to go back and take them. And whoever works in the field, let him not even care to take his garments which he took off during his work. And matters will be very hard on the pregnant women and the nursing mothers who carry children during the flight. And Christ calls them to pray that the circumstances of the flight be easy, for how hard the flight is in winter and the bitter cold.

13.8.1.en: My beloved brother ... spiritual flight from evil and uncleanness is the goal of all God's children, and Christ here offers you places where you can take refuge, for the mountains point to height and rising above the desires of the world. And taking nothing out of the house means not caring about material hoarding. And not turning back means steadfastness in repentance and leaving the old sins. And prayer is the constant weapon that accompanies us until our flight is complete and we settle with God in His Kingdom ... Amen.

13.9.0.en: Indeed, the tribulation of the destruction of Jerusalem was very great, for Titus destroyed more than one and a quarter million Jews (in the estimate of Josephus the Jewish historian, one million three hundred and fifty thousand Jews) from Jerusalem and its surroundings. And of course, this scale of destruction had not been known before in this region.

13.10.0.en: It is from God's tenderness that He made the days of the siege no more than five months, to give a chance to the elect, that is, the Christians, to escape with their lives.

13.10.1.en: Note: the explanation of verses 19 (and 20) also applies to the last days, for the persecution of the last time will be severe. But God's love shortens these days for the sake of the escape of everyone who holds fast to his faith.

13.11.s.en: (5) The signs of the end of the world and its events

13.11.0.en: The Lord Christ warns us of the appearance of false pretenders who claim to be the Christ, and Satan will support them, so they will bring satanic miracles and wonders, in order to confuse the believers into leaving the faith and following these deceivers, and Christ's word is clear: "believe it not" regarding these liars.

13.11.1.en: And therefore, we must not rush after any current outside the Church and the spirit of the Holy Bible, however great the miracles of these may be, but let the words of the Lord Christ always be with us: "But take ye heed: behold, I have foretold you all things", and we must keep to prayer, humility, deliberation and obedience to the Church, for these are the best guarantee of escape from the tricks of the deceiver.

13.12.0.en: "But in those days": that is, before the second coming of Christ, and not the destruction of Jerusalem.

13.12.1.en: "The sun ... the moon": the darkening of the sun and the moon has more than one meaning:

13.12.2.en: The first: which is the direct meaning, a reference to the end of the material world with its order which God established, and which depends on the sun and the movement of the planets around it.

13.12.3.en: The second: that because of the appearance of Christ with His mighty light, the sun appears dark in comparison with Him.

13.12.4.en: The third: which is the symbolic meaning, that is, after the spread of faith in Christ, the heretics distort the concepts of the faith and scatter the simple, so their minds (the sun) and their hearts (the moon) are darkened.

13.12.6.en: Scientifically: this phenomenon has begun to occur, as some great stars have disappeared from the universe.

13.12.7.en: Spiritually: the falling of many of the believing and famous Christians, like stars, into error, innovations and heresies.

13.12.8.en: "The powers that are in heaven shall be shaken": perhaps what is meant here is the elements of nature in the visible heaven, which St. Peter mentioned in his second epistle (2 Pet 3:10) "and the elements shall melt with fervent heat".

13.13.0.en: The Lord Christ describes the scene of His second coming, for as He ascended and a cloud received Him, so He will come also in the clouds with great power and glory, that is, with majesty and power and His divine authority, and with His glory which none can approach, and the cloud usually symbolizes the divine presence as happened in the days of Moses (Ex 13:21-22), and Solomon (1 Kgs 8:10-11), and at the transfiguration also (Mt; 17:5, Mk; 9:7, Lk 9:34). And God sends His angels and gathers His elect, that is, those who believe in His name and have escaped the great tribulation, from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven, that is, all the regions of the earth.

13.14.0.en: Christ here gives a parable, whose meaning is: just as you can distinguish some matters from their signs, such as the fig tree's blossoming with its leaves, so you know that summer is near, so also when you see all that I have told you, know that the destruction of Jerusalem and the end of the world has become very near.

13.15.0.en: This is what indeed took place in regard to the destruction of Jerusalem in the year 70 A.D., since most of the disciples and believers were alive and witnessed what happened.

13.15.1.en: And the Lord Christ concludes with an assurance that removes all doubt from His words, when He said that the passing away of heaven and earth is easier to believe than that one word of His should pass away.

13.15.2.en: My beloved God ... the signs of Your second coming are terrifying and frightening signs. And yet, I continue in my distance from You, occupied with the matters of this perishing world!!

13.15.3.en: Make me, my God, always remember Your coming in great glory, and gather me, with those whom Your angels gather, into Your embrace ... convert me, Lord, and I shall be converted.

13.16.0.en: As for the time and hour of Christ's second coming and the end of the world, it is not for anyone to know it or to strive to know it, since God made this hour in His authority alone, and did not declare it even to the angels; and even Christ did not declare it to any of mankind during His Incarnation.

13.16.1.en: And Christ makes clear the wisdom of hiding this appointed time from mankind, which is constant preparation, watchfulness and spiritual alertness, for if people knew that the time was still far off, their hearts would grow lukewarm and they would leave the life of repentance and preparation (see the comment and explanation at the end of the chapter: Did the Son not know the time and the hour?)

13.17.0.en: The Lord Christ here gives a parable by which He confirms the necessity of spiritual watchfulness and care for the salvation of the soul, for Christ Himself is God the Lord, the master of the house, who took a far journey, that is, ascended to heaven after the redemption, and left His house, that is, His Church, to His servants who believe in His name, and gave them gifts and authority, besides His commandments, and assigned to each one his work, to serve in His house according to the gifts distributed to them, and charged the porter, that is, the shepherds and priests, to watch and keep spiritual vigil over His servants.

13.18.0.en: The Lord Christ gives at the end of the parable a commandment, which is: "Watch", and warns us that "ye know not" the time of His coming.

13.18.1.en: "At even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning": according to Roman timekeeping, the Romans divided the night into four parts, from sunset to sunrise, that is, twelve hours, each part being three hours. And these parts were called elsewhere the first, second, third and fourth watch, and the word watch means a division or part. And the whole fear is that the Son of God will come and find people asleep in their sins, turned away from caring for the salvation of their soul, so there will be escape for no one. And Christ ends His words with the statement that this warning and admonition about the necessity of watching is not for His disciples only, but for all His servants who believe in His name in the whole world.

13.18.2.en: An important comment on (v. 32): does the Son know the hour of His coming or does He not know it?! And why did He say: "neither the Son, but the Father"?!

13.18.3.en: The Church teaches us an important principle, which is that any difficult verse in the Holy Bible is not taken alone, but is interpreted in the light of the rest of the texts of the Bible, as we shall follow in our explanation of this verse ... for Christ, as the heavenly Son of God, of course knows the hour, and the following verses prove that:

13.18.4.en: 1) "All things that the Father hath are Mine" (Jn 16:15): so if the Father possesses all knowledge, the Son possesses it also.

13.18.5.en: 2) "I and My Father are one" (Jn 10:30), "I am in the Father, and the Father in Me ... I am in the Father, and the Father in Me" (Jn 14:10, 11), verses that give the same meaning. (Notice the emphasis in the repetition of the last two verses).

13.18.6.en: (3) How can He be the Creator and not know when His creation ends?! "All things were made by Him; and without Him was not any thing made that was made" (Jn 1:3). (4) How can all judgment be His, and He not know when He judges? "For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son" (Jn 5:22), and also: "And yet if I judge, My judgment is true: for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent Me" (Jn 8:16).

13.18.7.en: (5) If we take the verse literally, then the Son also withholds knowledge from the Holy Spirit, and this is impossible, "for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God ... Even so the things of God knoweth no man, but the Spirit of God" (1 Cor 2:10-11).

13.18.8.en: Therefore, what is meant by this verse is: that Christ, as the Son of Man, and as a man representing all mankind, forbids all people to know this hour and to concern themselves with searching into it, and directs us to attend to repentance and the acceptance of His redemption. We can also say: that Christ knows the hour and the time, and the negation here comes to mean non-disclosure. An example: as when the students ask the teacher about the exam questions, and he answers that he does not know, and the not knowing here means not disclosing, since he himself is the one who set the exam.

13.18.9.en: The Last Supper, the arrest of Christ and His trial
